dod_intent_evidence: US Army contract awarded (Feb 2026) to build swarming attritable sUGVs for the 1st Cavalry Division, stemming from an xTechOverwatch competition win — see News section (3 independent defense trade outlets).
score_evidence: Entire homepage is combat/ops framed: 'Built for Combat...Proven against dust, heat, vibration, and shock. IP6 sealed...Field-hardened for the harshest combat environments' → very low lab_language_intensity
'ANTSNet: Field-proven autonomy stack...ATAK app, Triple redundant comms' explicitly names ATAK and comms redundancy for degraded environments → very low deployment_awareness_absence

'One operator. Multiple robots. Infinite tactical advantage'...'integrating into human formations now'...'Seamless fit with maneuver C2 structures' → very low operator_absence (operator/human-teaming is the central design frame)

Open roles skew heavily manufacturing/hardware (Production Technician, Manufacturing Technician, Lead Manufacturing Engineer, Mechanical Engineer) alongside swarm/software roles, not researcher-only → low hiring_profile_skew

Fresh $13M Seed (Feb 2025) funding a 31-35 person team now executing a live Army evaluation contract for the 1st Cavalry Division stemming from a single competition win (xTechOverwatch) → stage_pressure (classic valley-of-death timing: evaluation contract, tiny team, unproven path to program of record)

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Web app' and 'ATAK app' are named as delivery surfaces with no ATO/RMF/STIG language anywhere in the pack
blind_spots.operator_reality: A web app meant to run on government/tactical networks needs an Authority to Operate before it can touch live tactical data — the SWaP-C and comms-hardening story is thorough, but the compliance pathway for the software layer is completely unaddressed
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team composition (talent from Nikola, Zoox, Toyota, ASU, CMU) skews hardware/autonomy engineering, not government compliance/ISSO
blind_spots.evidence_quote: ANTSNet: Field-proven autonomy stack enabling swarm control and human teaming. Web app, ATAK app, Triple redundant comms

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Now fielding UGV swarms to maneuver formations' overstates a single-division evaluation contract as fielded reality
blind_spots.operator_reality: The actual news shows one Army contract with the 1st Cavalry Division stemming from an xTechOverwatch win — that's an operational-evaluation award, not a program of record; the gap between the marketing claim and the evaluation-stage reality is exactly the advocacy-chain risk (one division championing it isn't adoption) that kills transitions when the contract clock runs out before a program-of-record decision
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Early-stage marketing needs to project traction to investors and future DoD customers alike, ahead of the actual acquisition milestone
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Military-grade swarm logic. Combat-ready hardware. Now fielding UGV swarms to maneuver formations.

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Triple redundant comms' addresses link redundancy but never states a bandwidth budget under jamming/denial
blind_spots.operator_reality: Three redundant links that are all equally bandwidth-hungry can all degrade together in a contested EW environment; the pitch stops at 'redundant' without the harder engineering claim of graceful degradation under denied/low-bandwidth conditions
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Redundancy is the easier, more marketable claim; graceful-degradation engineering under DDIL is a harder problem that isn't mentioned
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Field-proven autonomy stack enabling swarm control and human teaming...Triple redundant comms

opener_hook: Swarmbotics' Army contract for 1st Cavalry Division sUGVs came out of an xTechOverwatch win — is that evaluation funding already on a path to a program of record, or still single-division scoped?
what_they_do: Builds low-cost, attritable autonomous ground robot swarms (FireAnt UGV + ANTSNet autonomy stack with ATAK integration) for military C-UAS/ISR/EW missions, currently under an Army evaluation contract with the 1st Cavalry Division.
